notes: You need a hire car (North Shore and Kualoa). Parking in Waikiki costs 40 USD a night. TheBus costs 3 USD (Pearl Harbor 20/42). An Uber from the airport costs 35-45 USD.

Winter temperatures are 24-27°C. The North Shore has giant waves (watch from the shore), whales are around from December to April, and January to February is rainy. Christmas and New Year are the most expensive.
Bookings: Diamond Head (30 days ahead), Hanauma (2 days ahead at 07:00 HST), Pearl Harbor (8 weeks ahead, 1 USD). You will need an ESTA visa waiver.
Poke 12-16 USD, plate lunch 15 USD, shave ice 6 USD, malasada 2 USD, luau 150-200 USD. Tip 18-20% and add 4.7% tax. It is an expensive island.
Reef-friendly sunscreen is required (oxybenzone is banned). Keep 3 m from turtles and seals, or risk a fine. Aloha and mahalo.
Try Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, spam musubi (from 7-Eleven) and loco moco. Look out for the Zippy's chain.

stops.name: Diamond Head State Monument
stops.tips: The crater climb is 1.3 km (steps and a tunnel). It opens at 06:00, and foreign visitors must book 30 days ahead. 5 USD, best at sunrise.

stops.name: Leonard's Bakery
stops.tips: Serving malasada (Portuguese doughnuts) since 1952. Eat them hot, and expect a queue.

stops.name: Waikiki Beach
stops.tips: See the Duke Kahanamoku statue. Take a surf lesson (75 USD) or try an outrigger canoe. Kuhio Beach is calmer.

stops.name: Marukame Udon Waikiki
stops.tips: Cheap, fresh udon. The queue moves fast.

stops.name: Waikiki Sunset at Kapahulu Groin
stops.tips: Watch the sunset from Duke's bar or the pier. On Fridays at 19:45 there are fireworks at the Hilton.

backups.name: Duke's Waikiki
backups.tips: Beach bar with hula pie, and a good sunset spot.

backups.name: Honolulu Zoo & Kapiolani Park
backups.tips: A park and zoo at the end of Waikiki, a good alternative to the beach.

stops.name: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
stops.tips: Book the boat programme to the USS Arizona Memorial on recreation.gov (1 USD). Slots open 8 weeks ahead at 08:00 HST and sell out. Bags are not allowed. Take bus 20 or 42.

stops.name: USS Missouri Battleship
stops.tips: The deck where Japan surrendered. A shuttle runs from Ford Island.

stops.name: Iolani Palace
stops.tips: The only royal palace in the US. See Queen Liliuokalani's prison room, and take the audio guide.

stops.name: Chinatown Honolulu
stops.tips: Browse the lei (flower garland) shops and Maunakea market. Come back for The Pig and the Lady in the evening.

stops.name: Tamashiro Market
stops.tips: A pink fish market in Kalihi. Try a poke (raw tuna) bowl, and bring cash.

backups.name: The Pig and the Lady Chinatown
backups.tips: Vietnamese-Hawaiian fusion. Try the pho at lunch.

backups.name: Bishop Museum
backups.tips: Hawaiian and Pacific culture, with feathered cloaks and a planetarium. An alternative to the palace.

stops.name: Hanauma Bay
stops.tips: A snorkelling reserve inside a crater. Book online 2 days ahead at 07:00 HST; slots vanish in seconds. Closed Monday and Tuesday. 25 USD plus 3 USD parking. Turtles and fish.

stops.name: Makapuu Lighthouse Trail
stops.tips: A 3 km paved path to the lighthouse. Look for whales (December to April) and views of Rabbit Island.

stops.name: Kalapawai Market Kailua
stops.tips: Beach market in Kailua with sandwiches, open since 1932.

stops.name: Lanikai Beach
stops.tips: One of the world's most beautiful beaches: turquoise water and the Mokulua Islands. Kayaks for rent. Parking is hard, so walk.

stops.name: Lanikai Pillbox Hike
stops.tips: A steep 30-minute climb up Kaiwa Ridge. Bunker views, and good at sunset.

backups.name: Kailua Beach
backups.tips: Lanikai's wider neighbour, with easy parking.

backups.name: Buzz's Lanikai
backups.tips: A steakhouse opposite the beach since 1962, and a favourite of Obama.

stops.name: Haleiwa Town
stops.tips: A surf town. Try shave ice at Matsumoto Shave Ice (1951), and expect a queue.

stops.name: Laniakea Turtle Beach
stops.tips: Green sea turtles come ashore here. Stay 3 m away; volunteers are on hand.

stops.name: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck Kahuku
stops.tips: The legendary truck for garlic shrimp plates, in Kahuku. Bring cash.

stops.name: Waimea Bay
stops.tips: Giant winter waves (November to February). Watch the surf competitions at Sunset and Pipeline.

stops.name: Sunset Beach
stops.tips: Come for the sunset. It is next to Pipeline, with surfers in the water.

backups.name: Ted's Bakery Sunset Beach
backups.tips: Chocolate haupia (coconut) pie and plate lunch.

backups.name: Waimea Valley
backups.tips: A botanical valley with swimming at the waterfall (life jacket provided). An alternative to the bay.

stops.name: Kualoa Ranch
stops.tips: The Jurassic Park valley. Book a UTV, horse or bus film tour online. Take in Kaaawa Valley and views of Chinaman's Hat.

stops.name: Kualoa Regional Park
stops.tips: A public park opposite Chinaman's Hat (Mokolii). Good for a picnic.

stops.name: Byodo-In Temple
stops.tips: A replica of Kyoto's Byodo-In, at the foot of the Koolau Mountains. Look for the bell and koi.

stops.name: Ho'omaluhia Botanical Garden
stops.tips: A free garden with views of the mountain wall. The famous road photo is not allowed, so go on foot.

stops.name: Ono Seafood Kapahulu
stops.tips: The city's best poke. Order the shoyu ahi, and bring cash.

backups.name: Waiahole Poi Factory
backups.tips: A traditional Hawaiian plate (kalua pork, poi, laulau), next to Kualoa.

backups.name: Nuuanu Pali Lookout
backups.tips: A windswept cliff view and the site of the 1795 battle. A good stop on the way back instead of the garden.

stops.name: Manoa Falls Trail
stops.tips: A 2.5 km rainforest walk to a 45 m waterfall. Expect mud, and spot the Lost set.

stops.name: Waiola Shave Ice
stops.tips: Shave ice since 1940. Try the Obama Rainbow, in Kapahulu.

stops.name: KCC Farmers Market
stops.tips: Saturday farmers market below Diamond Head. On other days, see the Kakaako murals (SALT).

stops.name: Ala Moana Beach Park
stops.tips: The locals' beach, with calm, reef-protected water. Watch the sunset at Magic Island.

stops.name: Luau Evening Waikiki Starlight
stops.tips: Hawaiian dance, fire knife and kalua pork, at the Hilton or Paradise Cove (Ko Olina).

backups.name: Highway Inn Kakaako
backups.tips: Hawaiian food since 1947. Try the laulau and pipikaula.

backups.name: Kakaako SALT Murals
backups.tips: The POW! WOW! graffiti district, an alternative to the market.

days.theme: Morning swim and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Kaimana Beach Sans Souci
stops.tips: The quiet end of Waikiki. Locals swim here, with views of Diamond Head.

stops.name: Koko Head Cafe
stops.tips: Lee Anne Wong's brunch spot in Kaimuki. Order the cornflake French toast.

stops.name: Ala Moana Center
stops.tips: An open-air mall for souvenirs (Kona coffee, macadamia nuts) and Foodland poke.

stops.name: HNL Airport Taxi
stops.tips: 25 minutes by Uber. There is an agricultural check (no fruit), then farewell.

backups.name: Foodland Ala Moana Poke
backups.tips: A supermarket poke counter. Have a farewell bowl.

backups.name: Ala Moana Beach Morning
backups.tips: A long beach run, instead of Kaimana.
